profile.reading: Data Foundry is a privately held Texas colocation operator. This facility, formally labeled Data Foundry 00 and marketed as Austin 1, sits at 7401 East Ben White Boulevard, Suite 1000, Austin, Texas 78741, in Travis County, roughly 2.5 kilometers from the operator's separate Data Foundry 01 and 02 buildings on the shared Data Ranch campus, confirming it as a genuinely distinct third Austin facility rather than an alternate name for either of those. The operator's own dedicated page describes the building at 40,000 square feet, with three 1,500 kW Caterpillar diesel generators providing 4.5 MW of combined backup generation capacity; that figure describes backup generation rather than a certified critical-IT-load rating, so it is not recorded here as critical_it_mw. Data Foundry has operated in Texas for more than two decades, with its current portfolio concentrated in Austin (this facility plus the separate Data Foundry 01 and 02 buildings on the Data Ranch campus) and one Houston facility (Houston 2, tracked separately in this registry); unlike larger REIT-owned or private-equity-backed operators, Data Foundry remains an independent Texas company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's specifications are sourced solely to the operator's own published materials. No year-opened date or independently audited MW figure was located for this facility in sourcing reachable this session. East Ben White Boulevard sits south of downtown Austin along US-71, a corridor that has drawn a mix of light-industrial, logistics, and technology tenants distinct from the Domain/North Austin corridor favored by some larger hyperscale and colocation developments in the metro. Data Foundry's decision to operate three separate, non-adjacent Austin facilities rather than consolidating onto a single campus reflects a disaster-recovery-minded design philosophy the operator markets directly to customers seeking intra-metro redundancy without the latency cost of an out-of-state secondary site.

reading.body:
Data Foundry Austin 1 occupies 40,000 square feet of technical space in Travis County, Texas. The operator has not published a power figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical load, or UPS capacity is on record here. Without a megawatt number, no rack-count or accelerator estimate can be responsibly derived.

The absence of a published power figure also places this campus outside the 13 Texas facilities for which this site holds capacity data, meaning it does not contribute to the 389 MW total mapped across the state. The state context ranks it 14th by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects the absence of a figure rather than a measured position, because any facility without a published number sorts below all 13 that have one. Texas has 133 mapped facilities in total, and the majority of those publish no power specification, so Austin 1 is typical of the state in that regard.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI workloads, the 40,000 square feet of technical space signals a mid-sized colocation facility rather than a hyperscale build, but floor area alone does not determine AI suitability. Power density per rack and total available power are the constraints that govern whether a site can support GPU clusters, and neither figure is published here. Until the operator publishes a power specification, this campus cannot be evaluated against the grid-constrained scaling thesis that defines AI infrastructure relevance.
